note: David's mapping: the 5 fundamentals nest under the 3 skills.

fundamentals.description: Creating and adjusting edge angle through inclination (whole-body lean) + angulation (joint bend, e.g. knees).
fundamentals.name: Edge angle control
fundamentals.tells: Skis skidding when grip was wanted, or catching an edge.

skills.name: Edging
skills.summary: Tipping the skis onto their edges to grip the snow.

fundamentals.description: Steering with the legs while the upper body stays quiet and facing downhill.
fundamentals.name: Rotary control (leg steering with separation)
fundamentals.tells: Whole-body rotation, shoulders turning with the skis.

skills.name: Rotary
skills.summary: Independent steering of the legs from the upper body. The legs turn the skis underneath a quiet, stable torso (upper/lower body separation). What most people call "turning" is a blend of rotary + edging, not a separate skill.

fundamentals.description: Staying balanced over the middle of the skis via ankle flexion — shins in contact with the boot fronts, CoM over the base of support.
fundamentals.name: Fore/aft pressure control (centered stance)
fundamentals.tells: Quads burning, sitting back, arms flailing.

fundamentals.description: Directing balance/pressure toward the outside ski of the turn, ski to ski.
fundamentals.name: Foot-to-foot pressure (lateral balance)
fundamentals.tells: Leaning into the hill, weight stuck on the inside ski.

fundamentals.description: Increasing/decreasing pressure smoothly as the turn develops (flex/extend).
fundamentals.name: Pressure magnitude regulation
fundamentals.tells: Bracing, sudden edge sets, "park and ride."

skills.name: Pressure
skills.summary: Managing force at the ski/snow interface — fore/aft, foot to foot, and how much.
